C13, three approved shell differences on the 404 page, named individually because the comparator keys one fingerprint per route and field. (1) body:preload-data is dropped: the attribute is SvelteKit-only, and this Slice 1 shell's native anchors deliberately perform no speculative data prefetch while client navigation stays deferred. (2) meta:robots=noindex is ADDED by Next; the baseline has no such meta and a 404 belongs out of the index, so the candidate is better here, not different-and-worse. (3) link:<bundle> is present on the candidate and absent from the baseline, and this one is a CAPTURE ARTIFACT rather than a candidate defect: 404.html is the one baseline page spelling its asset paths absolutely, extractFields() has always skipped /_app/ in exactly that spelling, so its stylesheets were never recorded. Both pages ship CSS. Widening the skip to erase the marker was rejected because it would make total stylesheet loss invisible everywhere, which control 27 exists to prevent. Every other shell element on this route matches the baseline exactly. Recorded in 3b projects/brandonwie.dev/actives/nextjs-migration/verification/contracts/C13-document-shell.md.

C8 finding 4: the SvelteKit /ko/feed page ships <html lang="en"> because src/hooks.server.ts substitutes %lang% from Paraglide's url strategy and vite.config.ts urlPatterns has no /feed pattern, so the KO page falls through to the base locale (one of the seven KO pages the C13 record names). The candidate ships lang="ko", which is the URL locale and what assert-c13-shell.ts row 1 requires of every candidate page. The baseline value is a defect carried by the Svelte site, not a contract. Recorded in 3b projects/brandonwie.dev/actives/nextjs-migration/verification/contracts/C8-feeds-redirects.md (finding 4).

C11 ships EN /system/3b, which makes this route an intersected page whose shell is compared for the first time. ONE normalized difference, and it is the same decision already approved on the six other routes: body:preload-data="hover" is dropped. The attribute is SvelteKit-only and has no Next equivalent; this shell uses native anchors and performs no speculative prefetch, with client navigation and its prefetch policy deferred until that surface is ported. The RAW shells differ in four classes, three of which normalizeShell (migration-verify.ts:637-665, applied by compare() at :736) absorbs before any diff is taken, so they are NOT part of this approval: (a) favicon and manifest hrefs — the baseline emits document-relative ../favicon.svg from this depth-2 route while the candidate emits /favicon.svg; normalizeShell resolves every non-absolute href against the page directory, so both land on the same absolute path. (b) the Google Fonts href — & against &; normalizeShell decodes attribute entities, so the two converge. (c) bundler asset filenames — three SvelteKit chunks against one Next chunk; normalizeShell drops every bundle-prefixed asset and emits the single presence key link:<bundle> instead. (d) body:preload-data — the one class normalization does NOT absorb, and therefore the one this entry approves. What is NOT approved here: the field-level differences on this route from the partial port (System3bPage stats, subsystems, evolution and blog-series sections are Slice 4). Those are expected progress that must disappear, and ledgering them would approve a difference that is supposed to go away. Recorded in 3b projects/brandonwie.dev/actives/nextjs-migration/verification/contracts/C11-library-ports.md. Line anchors are given for the function as a whole rather than per clause: the per-clause anchors in an earlier revision of this entry were wrong in two of three cases, and a range that moves with the function is harder to get wrong than a line that does not.
